questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

__Does it__ difficult to drive a lorry through a crowded narrow lane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Isn't it.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment is a question, and it requires an auxiliary verb to form a grammatically correct sentence.
 
• The auxiliary verb "does" is used to form questions in present tense for third-person singular subjects (he, she, it).
 
• **However, the subject in this sentence is "it," which is not a person, and therefore, the correct auxiliary verb to use is "is."**
 
• The contracted form "isn't it," is the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
 
• The correct sentence will be:
 
 
• Isn't it difficult to drive a lorry through a crowded lane?
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Option 1 (Aren't it) is grammatically incorrect because "aren't" is a contraction of "are not," which is not the correct auxiliary verb to use with the subject "it."
 
• Option 2 (Do it) is grammatically incorrect because "do" is not the correct auxiliary verb to use in this sentence, and it changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Option 4 (Would it) is grammatically incorrect because "would" is not the correct auxiliary verb to use in this sentence, and it changes the meaning of the sentence. It implies a hypothetical situation rather than a present situation.
